meta.title: An Email About a Football Quiz

paragraphs: Subject: Our Football Quiz. Dear Alex, Thank you for your email about your robot. It sounds great! I hope that you are well, and I hope that your robot works. I have some news, too. Ben and I made a quiz game for English class.

Teacher Nick teaches English to our class, and he gave us two weeks for the work. We worked on it every day after lunch in the computer room. Teacher Nick wanted a quiz about vocabulary. We chose football words like "goal", "corner", and "pass". Ben likes football more than I do, so he knew many words. Ben wrote forty questions. I made the design. First, I chose a green background, like a football field. Then I drew a small ball in each corner. The design took more time than the game itself. The game itself is simple. You read a word, and you click on its meaning.

We put the quiz on a school computer, and we gave it a password. The password is a secret, so I cannot tell you! On Monday, Ben forgot it, and we could not open the game. Teacher Nick laughed and helped us. Teacher Nick says, "A good password is long." Now we write the password in a small notebook. I always remember the notebook now.

On Tuesday, our class played the quiz. They played in pairs, and each pair had five minutes. Teacher Nick said, "Please be polite when you write a comment." A girl wrote, "Good game! Can I try again?" That is a polite comment. Everybody in class wanted a turn, so we made a list of names. A boy wrote, "Too hard!" Ben laughed, and he made two questions easier. We got twenty comments, and most were nice.

Do you play games on your computer? Please send me a photo of your robot. Maybe your robot can play football one day! If you want, I will send you our quiz. Then you can try the football words. Which words do you want in our next quiz? Best wishes, Tom.
text.summary: Tom writes an email to his pen pal Alex about a football vocabulary quiz that he and Ben made for English class. The email tells about the design, the password, and the polite comments.
